............ A very warm welcome to all our visitors ...........
Our school is situated in the rural village of Peasmarsh, near to Rye and was built by the Church in 1841. Our pupils mainly come from the village and surrounding areas. We make the most of our environment and are proud to provide children with a Forest School as well as large outdoor spaces, including 2 adventure trails and a pond. Our Christian ethos is part of everyday life at Peasmarsh - we look after everyone in our school community and our school feels like a family. We have high aspirations for all our pupils and support everyone to flourish as individuals, discovering their talents and unique abilities along the way.
Come for a visit
We would love you to come and see our classes in action and to talk to us about the teaching and learning here at Peasmarsh.
We are proud to be a Church of England school and invite you to feel the warmth of our Christian community.
Please ring on 01797 230325 or email the school office on office@peasmarsh.e-sussex.sch.uk if you would like to visit.
Please also look on our facebook page for more information about what the children have been getting up to.

All children have access to Religious Education at Peasmarsh. Although we are a Church of England school, the children learn about Christianity alongside other world religions. This helps pupils develop an understanding of themselves and others and promotes the spiritual, moral, social and cultural development of individuals, groups and communities.

Art and Design at Peasmarsh
At Peasmarsh we teach all children Art and Design. This gives them a chance to express their ideas, build on their observational skills, gain confidence, promote feelings of self-worth and develop their creativity and imagination. For some children, it is also a therapeutic experience which offers them time to relax, explore and regulate in a safe environment.

Art and Design Curriculum Overview
We teach Art and Design combined with Design and Technology in a condensed curriculum. The overview has been designed to cover the skills and knowledge needed for both subjects.

Design Technology at Peasmarsh
At Peasmarsh CE Primary School, our children are provided with a design and technology curriculum which allows them to use their imagination and be creative through designing and making. They are taught to combine their creativity, designing and making skills with knowledge and understanding to enable them to design and make a product. Skills are taught progressively ensuring all children are able to learn and practice in order to develop as they move through the school. Discussion and feedback allows the children to adapt and improve their product, a key skill needed throughout their lives.

Mathematics at Peasmarsh
All pupils at Peasmarsh Church of England Primary School love their maths learning and see themselves as budding mathematicians. Maths is taught daily in year groups so that all children can have targeted teaching with immediate feedback and opportunities for 'mathematical talk'.
Mathematics Curriculum Intent Statement
Curriculum Overviews
Progression Statements
To learn mathematics effectively, some things have to be learned before others, e.g. place value needs to be understood before working with addition and subtraction, addition needs to be learnt before looking at multiplication (as a model of repeated addition). You will see this emphasis on number skills first, carefully ordered, throughout our primary curriculum. For some other topics, the order isn’t as crucial, e.g. Shapes and Statistics need to come after number, but don’t depend on each other. We try to mix these so pupils have as wide a variety of mathematical experiences as possible in each term and year.

Reading at Peasmarsh
We love reading at Peasmarsh. We read every day - with our friends, with our class or on our own. We read books about all sorts of things and we love stories. Our teachers read to us every day and we choose books from our library to enjoy.
Reading Curriculum Statement
Reading for Pleasure
We encourage the children to read simply for the pleasure and enjoyment of a story or a poem or to find out about the things they enjoy.
The school library is open most lunchtimes for children to choose books and browse the shelves.
They are also given opportunities to read in class on thier own or with friends and to be read to.
Reading at Home
We expect all our children to read at home and encourage parents to read with their children on a daily basis. As soon as children enter school, they have access to reading book, which starts, with picture stories in EYFS. Children are never to old to share a book. Here are some top tips to help you read at home.
It can be hard to choose books for your child when there are so many out there. If you would like some recommended reading then please click on the link and find the list appropriate to your child's school year. Links can also be found on the class pages https://schoolreadinglist.co.uk/
Word Reading (Phonics)
At Peasmarsh we follow the 'Sounds-Write' Systematic Synthetic Phonics Programme. Phonics is the prime strategy used when encountering new words to read.
Comprehension
When pupils read fluently, they focus on understanding the text rather than just decoding. Fluency is a bridge from word recognition to comprehension as children progress to becoming confident and independent readers.
Progression of Whole Class Quality Texts
Our learning journeys stem from high quality texts chosen to inspire and empower the children. Many of these are from the 'Power of Reading' resource which supports the literacy curriculum in developing reading comprehension leading into writing composition, and fosters a whole school love of reading.
Common Exception Words
Common exception words are words that appear commonly in both texts and spoken language, but may be harder to decode. Children will be expected to learn these over time and with practice so that they can recognise them on sight.
